key_insight: Instead of enlarging channel width to preserve reconstruction under heavy compression (which causes latent collapse), TC-AE increases and optimizes capacity in the token space of a ViT-based autoencoder, maintaining fidelity and generative quality with compact latents.
problem_solved: Latent representation collapse and degraded generative/reconstruction performance when existing deep-compression autoencoders increase channel counts or rely on complex multi-stage training to meet high compression ratios.
method: ViT-based encoder–decoder that explicitly operates on and restructures the latent token space rather than only expanding channel dimensionality.
Token-capacity mechanisms (e.g., adaptive token allocation / token reshaping) that increase representational slots while keeping per-token dimension small to avoid collapse.
Capacity-preserving training objective and lightweight modules that regularize token usage so single-stage training yields high-fidelity reconstructions at strong compression.
impact: Enables higher-compression autoencoders with better reconstruction and generative behavior without bloated channel counts or complex pipelines — useful for efficient image storage, transmission, and compact representation learning.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing encoder → token-capacity module → bottleneck tokens → decoder (highlight token flow vs channel expansion).
Chart: reconstruction quality (PSNR/LPIPS) vs compression ratio comparing channel-expansion baseline and TC-AE.
Illustration of token collapse vs preserved-token-diversity (heatmaps or attention maps) to show the preservation of information.
Icon set: small model footprint, single-stage training, improved fidelity, and faster inference.
paper_title: TC-AE: Unlocking Token Capacity for Deep Compression Autoencoders
paper_authors: Teng Li, Ziyuan Huang, Cong Chen, Yangfu Li, Yuanhuiyi Lyu
